clue.text: Cancel cuts-or so it might appear

indicators.note: the clue hints that the letters of cuts-or so, once jumbled, show what they might appear as

explanation.surface: Someone striking out a clipping, with an editor's 'cuts, or so' aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it might appear' is the anagram signal: the eight letters of CUTS OR SO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete a word by drawing a line through it is to annul or cancel it.

clue.text: Direct accusation

explanation.surface: A blunt, straight-out allegation.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to give them an instruction or command, and a formal accusation laid against someone is likewise this word.

clue.text: Considers the outcome is open

indicators.note: the result or outcome of reworking the letters of is open is called for

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up a question and concluding the result is still undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a view is to judge or reckon, as one who considers something to be so.

clue.text: It's odd about the cash squeeze

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other here

parts.note: odd means peculiar or weird
L stands for pounds sterling, British money or cash

explanation.surface: A peculiar remark on a financial or credit squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: L (the pound sign, from Latin libra) goes inside STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle someone is to squeeze their throat; a synonym.

clue.text: Given employment in a warehouse due to expansion

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words a warehouse due

explanation.surface: A warehouse taking on extra staff because it is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is tucked inside wareHOUSE DUe; 'to expansion' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to work has been employed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wasn't slow to accept bill at intervals

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: went fast, hurried along
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A quick customer happily taking the bill at regular stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set apart with gaps between them are placed at intervals.

clue.text: Stick in a remittance or take off?

indicators.note: in places the stick piece inside the payment piece

parts.note: money sent or paid, wages
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A question of whether to put money in or withdraw it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or satirise them, a comic imitation.

clue.text: Scorn to read and draw

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully, an old sense
to draw in or lure is to tempt

explanation.surface: Disdain expressed for reading and drawing as pastimes.
explanation.walkthrough: CON as 'read, study' is an old verb, much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for looking down on something.

clue.text: The sauce naturists forego

explanation.surface: Nudists skipping the salad topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad sauce is a vinaigrette or similar, and putting on clothes each morning is what nudists go without.

clue.text: A half-dozen signs for bird-cages

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
the Ram is one of the zodiac signs

explanation.surface: Six astrological symbols advertised for birdcages.
explanation.definitionFit: Large enclosures for keeping birds are bird-cages, a synonym.

clue.text: Band on the head

parts.note: a strip of hair cut straight across the forehead, read as a band on the head

explanation.definitionFit: Hair cut short over the forehead forms a band across the brow, so this is a fair description.

clue.text: GIs seen making a beginning

indicators.note: making signals the letters of GIs seen are formed into something new

explanation.surface: American soldiers watched setting out on something new.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Bible is about creation, and the word means an origin or start.

clue.text: Gullible English author

parts.note: green means naive or easily fooled

explanation.surface: A naive English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a famous English novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Deals she organised reveal a lack of capital

definitions.note: noun phrase for an adjective: lacking a head, the top or capital

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of deals she are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Business deals arranged by a woman expose a funding shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is a head (as of a column), so having none means being decapitated.

clue.text: A pushy individual in the Midlands

parts.note: one who shoves, a jostler

explanation.surface: A thrusting person living in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: Ashover is a village in Derbyshire, in England's Midlands region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashover is a Derbyshire village, so it is a place located in central England.

clue.text: Flash information about heel

indicators.note: about here means going round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a ship that heels leans over, or lists

explanation.surface: A news flash about a shoe heel.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'heel' is the nautical lean.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to sparkle or flash with light.

clue.text: On returning sleeps for a while

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for sleeps is read backwards

parts.note: short sleeps are naps

explanation.surface: Coming home and dozing for some time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time, as in a short life span, is a period or while.

clue.text: Worries and dashes around a ship

indicators.note: around means the dashes piece goes outside the ship piece

parts.note: to hare is to run fast or dash
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone fretting and rushing about a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or bother persistently is to harry or worry someone.

clue.text: A rise in the main very small

definitions.text: A rise in the main very small

parts.words: A rise in the main very small
parts.note: the main is the sea, and the smallest rise of its water level each month is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea; the rise is the swell of the tide at its least.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide of least range, at the moon's quarters, gives the smallest rise of the sea.

clue.text: The baggage involved in legal action?

parts.note: a lawsuit is a suit
a court case is a legal action

explanation.surface: Luggage that turns up in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling case for clothes is a piece of luggage or baggage.

clue.text: Parking in a former tip

indicators.note: in puts the parking letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking in a former rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is a summit, not a dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The top point or peak of something is its tip.

clue.text: Rich, firm, and very good

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
pious means devout, very good

explanation.surface: A wealthy, steady and virtuous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich in the sense of abundant or plentiful.

clue.text: This might well be nice to see

indicators.note: suggests the letters of nice to could be turned into something else

explanation.surface: A sign that would be pleasant to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or observe something is to see it.

clue.text: A beast's sheepish love note

parts.note: coy means shy or sheepish
O is love, a zero score in tennis
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An animal's shy love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie wolf of North America, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Torn about heartless woman showing dislike

indicators.note: about here means wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, to tear

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for woman is dropped

parts.note: she is any woman

explanation.surface: Someone ripped up over a cold-hearted woman, displaying displeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the H from SHE, leaving SE to go inside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aggrieved or bitter at something is to show dislike of it.

clue.text: A bloomer lads hope to rectify

indicators.note: rectify means to put right, so the letters of lads hope are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boys hoping to correct an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is a flower, not a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily of the Mediterranean, an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: The rowing man may get hit!

explanation.surface: An oarsman likely to be struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The oarsman nearest the stern sets the pace for the crew, and a blow or strike is also this word.

clue.text: Many have very fine plumage

parts.note: many birds have soft, fluffy feathers; the clue describes that fine plumage

explanation.definitionFit: The soft fine feathers of young birds are a kind of plumage.

clue.text: Enthusiasm for strong drink

explanation.surface: Zeal for hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest or vigour is one sense, and a distilled liquor such as gin is the other.

clue.text: Sleepy-come to as required

indicators.note: required suggests the letters of come to as must be rearranged as needed

explanation.surface: A drowsy person asked to wake up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a deep unconsciousness is an extreme form of sleepiness or torpor.

clue.text: Children taking exercise inside sweated

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: seed means offspring or children
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Kids sweating during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid oozing out slowly, as sweat does.

clue.text: Let on modish guy is really quite natural

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the following pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable
he is a man, a guy
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A landlord telling a trendy man that something is quite innate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic or innate is natural.
